small_guidance:
- Add larger BLOCK_SP configs (e.g. 128/256 with num_warps=8, num_stages=2-3) and try BLOCK_OC tiling so the GEMM tile is `(BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_SP)` rather than always full OC=64; smaller BLOCK_OC × larger BLOCK_SP may improve occupancy.
- Pre-pack weight as `[KH, KW, OC, IC]` (or `[KH*KW, OC, IC]`) at init time so the inner-loop weight loads are contiguous and reuse better — and consider hoisting the weight load outside (load all KH*KW*OC*IC into registers once if it fits, ~36KB for OC=64,IC=16,3x3).
- Try `tl.dot` with `(BLOCK_SP, IC) x (IC, OC)` orientation (transpose accumulator to `[BLOCK_SP, OC]`) since `tl.min` over OC=64 of a `[BLOCK_SP, OC]` tile reduces along axis=1 which often maps better; sweep num_stages 3-4.
large_guidance:
- Switch to a channels-last input layout (NHWC) and do an im2col-style GEMM where the K dimension is `IC*KH*KW=144` reduced in one fused inner loop (single `tl.dot`) instead of 9 separate small dots; this lets you use `BLOCK_M=BLOCK_SP=128`, `BLOCK_N=OC=64`, `BLOCK_K=144` in one mma.
- Make the kernel persistent across the spatial dimension — one program per (N, OC tile) iterates over output rows, reusing weight in registers and amortizing weight loads across many spatial tiles; fuse min+tanh+tanh in the epilogue per tile.
- Consider implicit-GEMM with halo-aware shared-memory staging: load an input row-block once and slide the 3-wide window in registers to compute three output columns per load, reducing redundant input gathers (each input pixel is read up to 9 times currently).
